entries.1499ec73b202976b: Calculated value: revenue for the latest fiscal period divided by the number of employees, calculated for each company, with the median taken for the industry. Revenue and the number of employees are the printed values in the annual securities report's "Trends in Key Management Indicators and Other Data." Industries with fewer than 10 companies covered are not listed.
entries.335c90ad8146bbfb: Another point is that this figure is not a ranking of efficiency. Revenue divided by the number of people is a figure that reflects differences in the shape of a business — what it sells and what assets and people it runs with. The "Figures" section of industry pages also shows total-based revenue per 1 employee as a calculated value. Reading from both the median and the total basis is how to use this feature.

The median for the 3,118 companies for which both were available was ¥42.58 million. On the other hand, dividing the total sales of all companies by the total number of employees gives ¥62.9 million, which is larger than the median. The picture changes between the total-based figure, which is pulled up by companies with large sales, and the median, which looks at a typical company.

entries.e04bd0da0618d0f0: Each company's figures are the revenue and number of employees for the same period printed in that company's report. Companies that prepare consolidated financial statements use consolidated figures, and companies that do not use non-consolidated figures, so the basis differs by company. Whether factories or stores are held by subsidiaries changes the scope of the figures even for the same business, so this mixture accompanies comparisons across industries.
entries.fcae3e179349b938: At the top are [[industry:trading|Trading Companies]] (¥116.48 million), [[industry:energy|Energy]], and [[industry:real-estate|Real Estate]], and at the bottom are [[industry:it|IT and Software]] and [[industry:human-resources|Human Resource Services]] (¥20.76 million). The difference between the top and the bottom is 5.61 times. In businesses such as trading companies, where the transaction volume of products becomes revenue as it is, and businesses run with equipment and assets, revenue becomes large relative to the number of people. Conversely, in businesses that provide human labor itself, revenue increases almost in proportion to the number of people, so the amount per 1 person becomes small.
